title_en: China Everbright Bank, Beijing Business Department v. Qiancun Department Store Shopping Center and Qiancun Science, Industry & Trade Development Company — enforcement of a notarized debt instrument
keywords_en: Civil; Loan contract dispute; Mortgage guarantee dispute; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Beijing; Legal person; Financial institution; Civil Procedure Law; Compulsory enforcement effect of notarized creditor's rights documents; Realization of mortgage; Support for plaintiff; Loan contract; Mortgage of land use rights; Notarization for compulsory enforcement; Auction of mortgaged property; Land use rights; Guarantee; Mortgage
full_text_en:
China Everbright Bank Beijing Business Department v. Beijing Qiancun Department Store Shopping Center and Beijing Qiancun Science, Industry and Trade Development Company — enforcement of notarized creditor's rights document

Execution Applicant: China Everbright Bank Beijing Business Department.

Legal Representative: Liu Bo, Manager of the said Business Department.

Execution Respondent: Beijing Qiancun Department Store Shopping Center.

Legal Representative: Qi Hong, General Manager of the said Shopping Center.

Execution Respondent: Beijing Qiancun Science, Industry and Trade Development Company.

Legal Representative: Wang Ping, General Manager of the said Company.

On October 11, 1996 and November 12, 1996, the Execution Applicant, China Everbright Bank Beijing Business Department (formerly known as China Everbright Bank Beijing Qianmen Business Department; hereinafter referred to as the "Business Department"), entered into two Renminbi loan contracts with the Execution Respondent, Beijing Qiancun Department Store Shopping Center (hereinafter referred to as the "Shopping Center"). The contracts stipulated that the Business Department would lend to the Shopping Center working capital loans of RMB 20 million and RMB 15 million, respectively, with agreed terms and interest. The contracts also stipulated that if the Shopping Center failed to repay the loans in accordance with the contracts, it voluntarily submitted to judicial enforcement. These two Renminbi loan contracts were examined by the Beijing Notary Public Office, which issued notarized instruments and respectively granted them enforceability in accordance with the law.

On November 12, 1996, the Execution Applicant, the Business Department, also entered into a "Real Estate Mortgage Contract" and a "Supplementary Agreement" with the Execution Respondent, Beijing Qiancun Science, Industry and Trade Development Company (formerly known as Beijing Yaxiya Data Technology Development Company; hereinafter referred to as the "Development Company"). The contracts stipulated that the Development Company would use the 2nd, 5th, and 7th floors (land area of 465.5 square meters, building area of 6,087.5 square meters) of the Qiancun Business Building, for which it held the land use rights and property ownership, as collateral to secure the principal, interest, liquidated damages, and other expenses under the two Renminbi loan contracts. The contracts stipulated that if the Execution Respondents, the Shopping Center and the Development Company, failed to perform their repayment obligations when due, they voluntarily submitted to judicial enforcement. The mortgage contract and supplementary agreement were examined by the Beijing Notary Public Office, which issued notarized instruments and granted them enforceability in accordance with the law. Thereafter, the Business Department and the Development Company completed the registration procedures for the real estate mortgage with the Housing and Land Administration Bureau of Chaoyang District, Beijing, and the mortgage contract formally took effect.

After the Execution Applicant, the Business Department, had respectively entered into the aforesaid Renminbi loan contracts and the real estate mortgage contract with the Execution Respondents, the Shopping Center and the Development Company, it loaned RMB 35 million to the Shopping Center as agreed. However, by the final repayment deadline of September 16, 1997, the Execution Respondent, the Shopping Center, had not performed the obligation to repay the principal and interest, nor had the Execution Respondent, the Development Company, performed its guarantee obligation in accordance with the contract. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 218, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Business Department applied to the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court for compulsory enforcement.

After examining the notarized creditor's rights document submitted by the Execution Applicant, which had been given enforceability by the notary public office in accordance with the law, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found that enforcement should be granted. It then, pursuant to Article 220 of the Civil Procedure Law, issued enforcement notices to the Execution Respondents, the Shopping Center and the Development Company, ordering them to perform the obligations determined by the notarized creditor's rights document within the specified period. It also published notices in newspapers including the Beijing Evening News, urging all execution respondents to perform their obligations before September 20, 1998. However, both execution respondents still failed to perform their obligations. In order to realize the creditor's rights of the applicant, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court decided to compulsorily auction the Development Company's properties used as mortgage collateral.

On October 31, 1998, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court entrusted Dingfeng International Auction Co., Ltd. with a public auction of part of the Development Company's properties. The properties were sold for RMB 42.18 million (RMB 180,000 above the reserve price), and the proceeds from the auction were used to satisfy the debts owed by the execution respondents to the execution applicant. Thus, the enforcement of this case was completed.
